messages.subject: Re: NA MargLogLik and low BGammaHat
messages.body_plain:
Thank you Mauricio!
My sample size is 131 in total, group0 = 36, group1=62, group2=33. If I run the same model in lavaan with MLR estimator and in blavaan with default priors, will the model fit and parameter estimate differ a lot? I tried and got quite different
1) model fit :
CFI: .920
BCFI: .802
2) regression coefficients (lavaan a1, a2....b3) (related to our research question whether there are group differences)
lavaan:  p value of  e1, b2, and b3 are smaller than .050
blavaan: 95% CI of a1, c12, f1,f2, e1, e2, b1, b2, and b3 do not contain zero.

                                  data = dat,

messages.body_plain:
Yuan

In general should be colse to teach other of the model is the same. I would recommend to use the function sem and bsem to make sure that the same underlying constraints are used. For example, I am not sure you are running the same model with the argument fixed.x=T . Can check with fitMeasures of the blavaan object to have the same npar as the lavaan object

Also, these fit indices should be compare to the "normal" indices not the MLR ones

Since you are not actually sunning a multiple group model what matters more is the total sample

Even with models like this, would recommended to use priors less wide as the deafult ones

Didnt you say in an earlier post that the CFI was higher?

ML is not neccesarily the "correct" answer, so replicating them is not the objective of BSEM. Differences in the parameters can also be related to the unrealistic expectation of ML that your 130 sample is asymototically correct (equivalent to infinetly large)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mauricio,

1) The argument fixed.x= T is used because I add groups as predictors. Otherwise, I got lavaan ERROR: unordered factor(s) detected; make them numeric or ordered: group1 group2
2)  previous model: the output of the blavaan object from my first email is higher and close to the fitMeasures of the lavaan object. After I closed R studio, I run the same model again, the model fit become worse and very different from the fitMeasures of the lavaan object. So I restarted R studio, tried many times, and still got different results.
3) I chose BSEM because my sample size is small and Bayesian estimation may work for small samples. I chose robust estimation in lavaan because the assumptions of normality is voilated and I have outliers. What do you think which analysis is better? I am thinking blavaan with default priors, blavaan with informative priors, lavaan with robust estimator etc.
4) the npar is different. What should I do?
lavaan: npar = 145
blavaan: npar = 115
> fitMeasures(fit.RICLPMpoEnjEff)

5) sem in lavaan:   lavaan WARNING: fit measures not available if model did not converge

https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#divergent-transitions-after-warmup

4: The largest R-hat is NA, indicating chains have not mixed.

Running the chains for more iterations may help. See

5: Bulk Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior means and medians may be unreliable.

Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bulk-ess

Running the chains for more iterations may help. See

Many thanks!
Yuan

> > > > > > > You can look at modification indices, but guven that you dont have an actual measurement model, might indicate to relase model constraints that could go agaiants the restrictions for theis model.

> > > > > > > ### modification indices

> > > > > > >   return(mods)

messages.body_plain:
Yuan

With MCMC the results will change a little bit between runs, due to MCMC error variability but should not change a lot.

The main difference is due to not be running the same model, as you have different number of parameters.

First, check between models and find what are the differences between them. Probably the fixed.x argument, you can give the same argument to blavaan and see if you get the same model. Can run it with very few iterations, just to see you have the right model.

Once you have the same model, I would recommend BSEM with weakly informative priors, these are good general applications for small sample sizes. Can get properly estimated models, that dont rely on the large sample assumption

messages.subject: Re: NA MargLogLik and low BGammaHat
messages.body_plain:
After I added the argument meanstructure = T, int.ov.free = T in blavaan, the npar is the same and model fit becomes close. Thank you so much Mauricio!

在2023年4月3日星期一 UTC+2 14:25:55<mauga...@gmail.com> 写道：
> Yuan
>
> With MCMC the results will change a little bit between runs, due to MCMC error variability but should not change a lot.
>
> The main difference is due to not be running the same model, as you have different number of parameters.
>
> First, check between models and find what are the differences between them. Probably the fixed.x argument, you can give the same argument to blavaan and see if you get the same model. Can run it with very few iterations, just to see you have the right model.
>
> Once you have the same model, I would recommend BSEM with weakly informative priors, these are good general applications for small sample sizes. Can get properly estimated models, that dont rely on the large sample assumption
>
>
>
> On Monday, April 3, 2023 at 11:17:11 AM UTC+2 huyy...@gmail.com wrote:
> > Hi Mauricio,
> >
> > 1) The argument fixed.x= T is used because I add groups as predictors. Otherwise, I got lavaan ERROR: unordered factor(s) detected; make them numeric or ordered: group1 group2
> > 2)  previous model: the output of the blavaan object from my first email is higher and close to the fitMeasures of the lavaan object. After I closed R studio, I run the same model again, the model fit become worse and very different from the fitMeasures of the lavaan object. So I restarted R studio, tried many times, and still got different results.
> > 3) I chose BSEM because my sample size is small and Bayesian estimation may work for small samples. I chose robust estimation in lavaan because the assumptions of normality is voilated and I have outliers. What do you think which analysis is better? I am thinking blavaan with default priors, blavaan with informative priors, lavaan with robust estimator etc.
> > 4) the npar is different. What should I do?
> > lavaan: npar = 145
> > blavaan: npar = 115

messages.body_plain:
After working on the example that you sent off-list, I just pushed a fix to github that might allow your model to run. Basically, blavaan runs lavaan for 1 iteration to initialize the model. That is why those lavaan-specific warnings show up. I made a change so that blavaan tries to keep going even if the 1-iteration lavaan run fails. Let me know if there are still problems.

There are instructions for installing from github at the bottom of this page:

https://ecmerkle.github.io/blavaan/

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Parallel execution
messages.body_plain:
İbrahim,

You could send each chain to a different core by adding this to your
bsem/bcfa/blavaan command:

bcontrol = list(cores = 3)

where the "3" could change if you are running more/fewer than 3 chains.

If you have a big dataset or big model, you might run the model on a
subset of the data or on smaller pieces of the model to ensure that
things are working correctly. Sometimes the model is slow because it is
not working correctly.

Ed

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I apologize if this is a naive message, but I'm wondering about blavaan convergence criteria for both target = "jags" and target = "stan"? Specifically: is it definitely the case that the iterations stop once all parameter PSRFs are <= 1.05 (i.e., Gelman & Rubin, 1992 and Brooks & Gelman, 1998), unless the user specifies otherwise?

I used this type of code:
    target = "stan"

then specified the null and desired models like this:
  Ind3.null.fit <- bcfa(Ind3.model_null, data=df)
  Ind3.CS.fit <- bcfa(Ind3.model_CS, data=df, dp=mydp, std.lv <http://std.lv>=TRUE)
  Ind3.CS.bfi <- blavFitIndices(Ind3.CS.fit, baseline.model = Ind3.null.fit)

I know I can ask for the PSRFs, but again, I'm wondering what the default stopping/convergence rule(s) is/are.

Thank you in advance!

Best,
Liz

messages.subject: Re: convergence = "auto" for JAGS
messages.body_plain:
Liz,

The documentation could indeed be improved here. For target="stan",
there is no built-in convergence criterion. The default is to run 500
warmup samples and then keep 1000 samples per chain. It does that
regardless of whether the chains converge. You could change the
behavior by manually setting the burnin and sample arguments of bcfa().

For fit indices or other metrics that involve the model log-likelihood,
it might be worth keeping more than 1000 samples per chain, to reduce
sampling noise. (i.e., so that the indices remain stable each time you
estimate the model)

For target="jags", you can also use the convergence="auto" thing, which
capitalizes on functionality from the runjags package. I don't think
this has been implemented for Stan, probably because the Stan samplers
tend to be better at converging as compared to Gibbs sampling.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: convergence = "auto" for JAGS
messages.body_plain:
Liz

For when I want to have it "automatically" stop, I recommend using a loop for increasing the number of iterations, but this means that the model might run multiple times, and can be time consuming if the model/data is large.
Important here, always keep the number of samples the same, so its easier to compare models, get fit indices, etc. can adjust the initial number of burn iterations, and the number of iterations to be added at each loop

In this case I am using Rhat < 1.05 as the convergence criteria, but in Stan they recommend Rhat < 1.01

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

BURN <- 1000
rhat <- 20
while (rhat > 1.05) {

  BURN <- BURN + 2000 ### increase burn in by 2000 iterations every time

  fit <- bcfa(HS.model, std.lv <http://std.lv>=T,
              data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
              n.chains = 3, burnin = BURN,
              sample=1000,target="stan")
  rhat <- max(blavInspect(fit, "psrf"), na.rm=T)
  print(paste0("Rhat=",rhat))
}

Hello! Sorry for coming back to this after a long time. I am wondering if there is any way to also convert from the stanfit object back to blavaan?

The issue that I have is that the maintainers of the high performance cluster at my university require each chain to be sent as a separate job to the cluster. For now, I can convert the individual blavaan fit objects to stanfit objects and then merge the stanfit objects with sflist2sf. However, it's much more convenient to work with a blavaan fit object than a stanfit object and I would like to convert the merged stanfit object to a blavaan fit object.

Alternatively, is there perhaps a way to merge the blavaan fit objects resulting from individual chains into a single blavaan fit object without converting it to stanfit object in between?

in blavaan, the stanfit object is held in the slot

messages.body_plain:
I dont usually use dummy variables as predictors like this. Because its hard to interpret what is the indirect effect and what is the indirect effect of the baseline groups. I would usually have group as a multiple group model, but that would be a moderation question, instead of mediation

These are the indirect effects of groups 2 compared to 0 group, and indirect of groups 3 to group 0. Not sure how meaningful this interpretation is?

Another option could be to include the 3 dummy code variables (no baseline group), and fixed the intercept of the outcome variables to 0. This way would estimate the paths for each group and you can define the difference between them. Havent use this approach for mediation, but I think it should work

messages.subject_clean: How to convert from blavaan object to a stanfit object?
messages.body_plain:
Mauricio is right that you could put this new object in
fit@external$mcmcout, and you might get correct ppp, waic, looic
values, but other model summaries will be incorrect (only using 1
chain).

It seems possible to create a function that allows what you want, but
it is not currently possible. If you add an issue to github as a
reminder, maybe we will get to it in the future.

One other thing: if you do not estimate the chains in parallel, it
seems that the maintainers of the cluster would not be able to tell
whether you are running 1 chain vs multiple chains. But maybe each
chain takes a long time, and they want to reduce the total runtime of
each job...

Ed

messages.subject: intercepts not printing?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am running several blavaan codes at the same time using parallel processing on a high-performance cluster with a colleague of mine, and we have run into the weirdest issue. On my "regular" computer I have no problem getting all of the parameter output to print out (with PSRFs included) but on the high-performance computer, sometimes the intercepts do not print, especially when I constrain 1 or more factor covariances.

I have not been able to replicate the problem on my regular computer...my regular computer is using R 4.2.2 but the high-performance cluster is using R 4.2.0. Is it possible that the small R version difference is the bug? Or possibly just a computer-specific memory allocation?

It is so odd, so I thought I'd see if anyone else has seen this occur before!

Best,
Liz

messages.subject: Re: intercepts not printing?
messages.body_plain:
Liz,

I would guess that you are running a newer version of blavaan on the cluster as compared to your regular computer. On newer blavaan versions, the intercepts are sometimes omitted if they would not change the model in any way. This is the same behavior as lavaan. If you always want the intercepts, specify

meanstructure = TRUE

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Split chain Rhat when JAGS is called
messages.subject_clean: Split chain Rhat when JAGS is called
messages.body_plain:
David, blavaan is reporting the Rhat that is output by the runjags package (also called "psrf"), which I believe uses a simpler computation.

To get what rstan does, you can use the code below (it assumes that fit is your fitted blavaan model).

You might double-check that rstan uses the computations you expect; sometimes rstan lags behind other Stan-related packages. But if you know a different function that does different computations, you should be able to send the draws object to that other function.

Ed

draws <- aperm(as.array(blavInspect(fit, 'mcmc')), c(1, 3, 2))
## add lavaan-like parameter names to posterior draws:
nmtch <- match(dimnames(draws)[[3]], parTable(fit)$pxnames)
dimnames(draws)[[3]] <- with(parTable(fit), paste0(lhs,op,rhs))[nmtch]

rstan::monitor(draws, warmup = 0)
